points: In the Chicago District the default time is 10 minutes. A default is claimed, not automatic, and the team that was on time may waive it.
Before anyone goes on court, the home captain names the official clock and says if the match is untimed, soft-timed or hard-stop.
Agree before the match: standard tiebreak or Coman tiebreak.

questions.q: In the Chicago District, how long after the scheduled start can a late player arrive before the opponent may claim a default?
questions.why: The default time is 10 minutes. If a player is not on court and ready to play 10 minutes after the scheduled start, the opponent may claim a default of that match.

questions.q: Your opponent arrives 12 minutes late. Is the match lost for them automatically?
options: No. Your team may claim the default, or waive it and play
Yes. The default is automatic after 10 minutes
No. A default can only be claimed after 20 minutes
Yes, unless the captains agree to a later start
questions.why: A default is claimed, not automatic. The team that was on time may waive it.

questions.q: Who names the official clock for the match, and when?
options: The home captain, before anyone goes on court
The visiting captain, before anyone goes on court
The players on each court, after the warm up
The club front desk, when time is nearly up
questions.why: Before anyone goes on court, the home captain names the official clock and says if the match is untimed, soft-timed or hard-stop.

questions.q: What is the difference between a soft-timed and a hard-stop match?
options: Soft-timed: a tiebreak in progress is finished. Hard-stop: play ends at the set time, full stop
Soft-timed: the timed procedure is not used. Hard-stop: it is used
Soft-timed: the warm up is shorter. Hard-stop: there is no warm up
There is no difference. They are two names for the same thing
questions.why: Both follow the timed procedure. In a soft-timed match any tiebreak in progress is played to the end. In a hard-stop match play ends at the set time.

questions.q: Besides the clock, what should you agree on before the match starts?
options: Whether set tiebreaks go to 7 or to 10
Who serves first in a tiebreak
How long the changeovers will be
questions.why: Agree before the match which tiebreak you use: standard or Coman.

questions.q: In a Coman tiebreak, when do you change ends?
options: After the first point, then every 4 points
Every 4 points, starting from the first point
questions.why: Coman: change ends after point 1 and then every 4 points. Standard: change every 6 points.

questions.q: You walk onto the court 6 minutes into the warm up. How much warm up do you get?
options: A full 10 minutes of your own
questions.why: The warm up is 10 minutes in total for the court, not per player. A player who shows up during it joins in and the clock is not extended.

questions.q: You win the racquet spin. What can you do?
options: Pick serve or receive, or pick the end, or make the opponent choose
Pick both who serves and which end
questions.why: The winner of the spin picks serve or receive, or the end, and the loser picks the other. The winner can also pass the choice to the opponent.

questions.q: You win the spin and choose to serve. What does your opponent get to choose?
questions.why: When the winner picks serve or receive, the loser picks the end.
